items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1962-04-11
items.q: Well, that band was the Golden Leaf. And Jesse Jackson was the manager. And I played with Jesse on the arm. Long time. Long time. Long years.

ctx.x: Happy. Let's see, this is the first reel, reel one. And what's today's date? It's April the... Let me see. Must be the 11th, huh? April the 10th. April the 10th. This is Wednesday. Yeah, and this is Wednesday, 1962. Okay, Lolly, you want to say something? Put your name. Okay, Marjorie Zander. Okay, my name is Dick Allen. We can check it now. See, when we stopped, when Russell and I were here, we stopped on Jesse Jackson. You just started telling us about that. Oh, yeah. What about that band? You just had…

Well, that band was the Golden Leaf. And Jesse Jackson was the manager. And I played with Jesse on the arm. Long time. Long time. Long years. And it was me, Jesse Jackson. Bud Russo. And the big Collins. And Arthur. A little Arthur. What did Arthur play? He played clarinet.
A little Arthur? What else? Did he play any other instruments? No other instruments. Just clarinet? Yeah.

items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: I went, I went and played with the Golden Laith Band, Jesse Jackson.

ctx.x: See? Did the guys improvise on the drums when you were a kid, or were they strictly reading?

Well, they used to improvise their whole life, because me, I used to improvise my canard. Mm-hmm. And then again, after I stayed with Amos Riley a long time, and that man broke up, I went, I went and played with the Golden Laith Band, Jesse Jackson. I stayed there.
